# Targeted discovery interview

Use only during interactive analysis or development when a decision remains that changes architecture, rollout, risk or acceptance. Read available code, task memory and relevant references first. Do not ask the user to rediscover facts available there.

Ask one question at a time. State the unresolved decision, recommend an option with its reason, and describe the significant consequence or trade-off of the alternative. Do not force a recommendation when evidence is insufficient; explain what is missing.

At the start of development Planning, use the [initial planning decisions](../workflows/development.md#initial-planning-decisions-and-system-impact) to identify unresolved material choices. These must enter the interview before the dependent plan is finalized; do not skip deployment order or service continuity merely because the final architecture is valid.

Reuse answers and approvals already provided. Stop the interview when the remaining uncertainty no longer affects the requested implementation. Do not demand exhaustive certainty or apply a fixed question count.

Record approved material decisions in the existing task record. An unanswered question is not approval. Continue independent safe work when possible; pause only the part dependent on the decision.

For automated review, do not run this interview. Report the missing evidence and its impact on review confidence without presenting an assumption as a confirmed defect.
